rationale: Edge-case lens (the only applicable lens under the compact profile plus the no-spec acceptance skip) surfaced two real defects in the new formatting code: StatusLabel.tsx's '=== 1' singular check breaks for a string-typed unique_users_count (CR-001), and helpers.ts's formatExactCount can render literal 'NaN' for a non-numeric value because it lacks the guard already present in the sibling formatMetricCount (CR-002). Two other candidates were dismissed as unreachable: the tooltip-target id/slug collapse (both fields are non-optional strings) and the unclamped negative-count path (mirrors the pre-existing, unclamped formatCompactCount; counts cannot legitimately go negative). No story/spec exists for this ticket, so acceptance did not run (genuine no-spec) and confidence is capped low; the compact profile does not expect a standards audit, so its three rows are recorded na with no coverage gap.

findings.title: Pluralization breaks for string count values
findings.problem: `const count = assistant.unique_users_count ?? 0` keeps the raw value even though `Assistant.unique_users_count` is typed `string | number`. The strict `count === 1` checks at lines 65 and 78 compare against the number 1, so a string count of `'1'` never matches.
findings.impact: A GLOBAL assistant with exactly one recorded use shows the grammatically incorrect 'uses'/'total uses' whenever the backend returns unique_users_count as a numeric string, which the field's own declared type permits and which the code never normalizes.
findings.recommendation: Coerce once at the source: `const count = Number(assistant.unique_users_count ?? 0)` at line 55, so formatMetricCount/formatExactCount and both `=== 1` checks operate on a consistent number.

findings.title: formatExactCount can render literal 'NaN'
findings.problem: `Number(value || 0).toLocaleString('en-US')` only falls back to 0 when `value` itself is falsy. A non-numeric truthy string (or anything where `Number(value)` is NaN) is passed straight to `.toLocaleString`, which formats NaN as the literal text 'NaN'.
findings.impact: The GLOBAL row's tooltip and aria-label ('{count} total use(s)') would display 'NaN total use(s)' to sighted and screen-reader users, unlike the sibling formatMetricCount, which already guards this exact case with `Number(value) || 0`.
findings.recommendation: Mirror formatMetricCount's guard: compute `const n = Number(value) || 0` first, then call `.toLocaleString('en-US')` on `n`.
